subject: Geography
description: Thar desert + Cold desert (Ladakh, Spiti); flora, fauna, people

questions.stem: India's MAIN HOT DESERT, the THAR, lies primarily in:

options.option_text: Punjab + Haryana states (north India)
Rajasthan (and parts of Gujarat, Sindh)
Madhya Pradesh + Chhattisgarh (central)
Tamil Nadu + Kerala (south India coast)

questions.explanation: THAR DESERT (also called GREAT INDIAN DESERT or MARUSTHALI) — covers ~200,000 sq km. Mostly RAJASTHAN (~60%), parts of GUJARAT (Kutch is partly desert), Pakistan (Sindh + Cholistan = ~80% of Thar in Pakistan side). 17th LARGEST desert in the world. INHA-INDIRA GANDHI CANAL (formerly Rajasthan canal) — brings water from Punjab rivers; helped agriculture in part of Thar. Climate: extreme — summer 50°C+; winter near freezing. Most population density of any desert — ~80 people/km² (Thar has historic towns: Jaisalmer, Bikaner, Jodhpur).

questions.stem: India's COLD DESERT region is in:

options.option_text: Sundarbans of West Bengal coast
Ladakh + Spiti valley (high altitude)
Tamil Nadu coastal area near sea
Kerala backwaters tropical region

questions.explanation: COLD DESERT — LADAKH + LAHAUL-SPITI valley (Himachal). High altitude (3000-5500 m). RAINSHADOW of Himalayas + Karakoram → very dry (<200 mm rainfall). Cold (winter −30 to −40°C; summer ~25°C). Sparse vegetation. Famous: HEMIS National Park (Ladakh — snow leopard habitat), Pin Valley NP (Spiti — Himalayan ibex, red fox), Tso Moriri + Pangong lakes. PEOPLE: Ladakhis + Tibetans (ethnic + cultural similarity); Buddhist monasteries (Hemis, Thiksey, Diskit). Famous DOUBLE-HUMP CAMEL (Bactrian camel) — Nubra Valley, only place in India.

questions.stem: ARAVALI RANGE (one of the oldest mountain ranges in the world) acts as a barrier to the eastward spread of:

options.option_text: Ganga river system in north
Thar desert (eastward expansion)
Brahmaputra river of north-east
Himalayan glaciers melting flow

questions.explanation: ARAVALI — one of OLDEST fold mountain ranges in the world (~3.5 BILLION years!). Highly eroded. Stretches from Gujarat (Pavagadh) → Rajasthan → Haryana → Delhi → up to ~700 km. Highest peak: GURUSHIKHAR (1722 m, Mt Abu). Acts as a NATURAL BARRIER preventing eastward expansion of Thar desert into Indo-Gangetic plain. DEFORESTATION + mining (illegal) of Aravali → desert is creeping into Haryana/Delhi. Famous places along Aravali: MOUNT ABU (only hill station in Rajasthan), ALWAR, RANTHAMBORE, UDAIPUR (in Aravali foothills). Mining banned in NCR Aravali area by SC.

questions.stem: INDIRA GANDHI CANAL, longest canal in India, brings water to Thar desert from:

options.option_text: Yamuna at Tajewala headworks (Haryana)
Sutlej-Beas (HARIKE BARRAGE) in Punjab
Ganga at Haridwar's main barrage works
Narmada at Sardar Sarovar dam (Gujarat)

questions.explanation: INDIRA GANDHI CANAL (formerly Rajasthan Canal; renamed 1984 after PM's death). Source: HARIKE BARRAGE in Punjab (confluence of Sutlej + Beas). Length: ~650 km — longest canal in India. Built in stages from 1958. Brings water to NW Rajasthan (Bikaner, Sri Ganganagar, Hanumangarh, Jaisalmer, Barmer, Churu) — turned a desert into a wheat / mustard / cotton-growing region. Dependent on Indus Water Treaty (1960) — eastern rivers (Ravi, Beas, Sutlej) granted to India. Critique: water-intensive irrigation in arid zone → waterlogging + salinity in some areas.

questions.stem: The 'GREAT INDIAN BUSTARD' (critically endangered bird) is found in:

options.option_text: Sundarbans of West Bengal
Thar desert + Kutch grasslands
Western Ghats rainforests
Eastern Himalayas of Sikkim

questions.explanation: GREAT INDIAN BUSTARD (Ardeotis nigriceps) — large-bodied (~1 m tall), brownish, ground-dwelling bird. State bird of Rajasthan. Habitat: arid + semi-arid GRASSLANDS of Thar (Rajasthan, esp. JAISALMER + DESERT NATIONAL PARK), Kutch (Gujarat — DABASIRI Sanctuary), Andhra/Maharashtra patches. CRITICALLY ENDANGERED — fewer than 150 left! Threats: habitat loss, electrocution from power lines (major cause; SC ordered transmission lines underground in some habitats), pesticides. Conservation: PROJECT GREAT INDIAN BUSTARD (Sariska + Desert NP, captive breeding at Sam, Jaisalmer). Known locally as GODAWAN.

questions.stem: RANN OF KUTCH is a unique ecosystem in:

options.option_text: Maharashtra (around Konkan coast)
Gujarat (large salt marsh on western coast)
Rajasthan (around Jaisalmer area)
Punjab (across Indo-Pak border)

questions.explanation: RANN OF KUTCH — vast salt marsh in KUTCH region of GUJARAT (NW India), borders Pakistan's Sindh. Two parts: GREAT RANN (~7500 sq km, north) + LITTLE RANN (~5000 sq km, south). One of largest SALT DESERTS in the world. Floods during monsoon (becomes shallow lake); turns to dazzling white salt flats in winter. Famous: WILD ASS (only home of Indian wild ass — Khur, Equus hemionus khur — in Little Rann). FLAMINGOS at Khadir Bet. RANN UTSAV — annual cultural festival (Nov-Feb), tents at Dhordo. Salt cultivation = livelihood. KUTCH = largest district in India by area.

questions.stem: The KHEJRI tree, sacred + state-tree of Rajasthan, is famous for:

options.option_text: Producing fragrant rose flowers
Drought-tolerant tree (lifeline of Thar)
Bearing apples + temperate fruits
Coniferous needle-leaf evergreen

questions.explanation: KHEJRI (Prosopis cineraria) — drought-resistant, very deep roots reaching ground water, leguminous (fixes nitrogen → enriches soil). Multipurpose: fodder (leaves), edible pods (SANGRI — cuisine of Rajasthan), fuelwood. STATE TREE of Rajasthan + Telangana. CULTURAL — sacred to Bishnoi community; CHIPKO origin point in 1730 KHEJARLI MASSACRE — 363 Bishnoi villagers killed by Maharaja's army for protecting khejri trees from being cut for palace construction. Led by Amrita Devi. Considered ONE of EARLIEST environmental movements globally — predates Chipko by 250 years!

questions.stem: Lake Sambhar in Rajasthan, India's largest inland saltwater lake, was designated a Ramsar Wetland of International Importance primarily because it serves as:

options.option_text: A wintering ground for flamingos and other migratory waterbirds
The primary source of the Luni River that drains the Thar Desert
An Indus Valley Civilisation site with major archaeological ruins
A freshwater reservoir supplying drinking water to Jaipur city

questions.explanation: Lake Sambhar was included in the Ramsar List in 1990, chiefly for hosting tens of thousands of flamingos and other migratory birds each winter, making it ecologically irreplaceable. The Luni River rises near Ajmer from the Aravalli hills, not from Sambhar. Sambhar is a saline lake and cannot supply drinking water. No major Harappan site has been excavated at Sambhar itself.

questions.stem: The Manganiyar community, celebrated for their desert folk music using the bowed khamaicha and the morchang jaw-harp, belongs to which social group of western Rajasthan?

options.option_text: A Muslim hereditary musician caste from Barmer and Jaisalmer districts
A Hindu Brahmin priestly community from the oasis towns of Bikaner
A tribal community of the Aravalli foothills specialising in oral epics
A nomadic Rajput warrior clan that adopted music after losing land rights

questions.explanation: The Manganiyars are a Muslim hereditary musician (mirasi) caste concentrated in Barmer and Jaisalmer districts, traditionally performing for Rajput patrons. They are distinct from the Langas, another Muslim musician group from the same region. They are not Brahmin, tribal, or Rajput by origin — the distractor about Rajput warriors losing land is a fabricated explanation with no historical basis.

questions.stem: Jaisalmer Fort, nicknamed 'Sonar Qila' (Golden Fort) and part of the UNESCO World Heritage hill-forts cluster, is architecturally distinctive among Rajput forts primarily because:

options.option_text: It was built by Emperor Akbar to defend against Mughal rivals in Sindh
It is one of the world's largest inhabited forts with residents living within its walls
It is constructed of pure white marble quarried from the Aravalli mountain range
It stands on the banks of the Luni River, giving it a natural water-based defence

questions.explanation: Built in 1156 CE by Rawal Jaisal on Trikuta Hill, Jaisalmer Fort is one of the world's largest 'living forts' — roughly 3,000–5,000 people including priests, merchants, and hoteliers still reside within its walls. Its golden hue comes from yellow Jurassic-era Trikuta sandstone, not white marble. Akbar did not build this fort; it predates him by over four centuries. The fort sits in the middle of the Thar Desert, far from the Luni River.

questions.stem: The Cold Desert Biosphere Reserve of Himachal Pradesh, covering the Pin Valley, Kibber Wildlife Sanctuary, and Spiti trans-Himalayan plateau, is designated primarily as habitat for which flagship species?

options.option_text: Snow leopard (Panthera uncia) and Himalayan ibex in high-altitude terrain
Bengal tiger and Indian one-horned rhino in sub-alpine grassland belts
Asiatic lion and Indian wild ass under the Project Lion conservation scheme
Red panda and clouded leopard in mid-altitude moist conifer forests

questions.explanation: The Cold Desert Biosphere Reserve (established 1992) at 3,000–6,000 m altitude is the key Indian stronghold of the snow leopard and Himalayan ibex (Capra sibirica), both highly adapted to extreme cold-desert conditions. Bengal tiger and one-horned rhino are confined to warm lowland forests (Assam, West Bengal). Asiatic lions exist only in Gir, Gujarat. Red panda and clouded leopard are species of northeastern India's wet subtropical forests — none of these are trans-Himalayan cold-desert animals.

questions.stem: Dhordo village near the Great Rann of Kutch received global acclaim in 2023 when it was selected as a 'Best Tourism Village' by which international body?

options.option_text: UNESCO (United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organisation)
UNWTO (United Nations World Tourism Organisation) at its General Assembly
UNEP (United Nations Environment Programme) for its ecotourism model
World Travel and Tourism Council (WTTC) at its annual global summit

questions.explanation: Dhordo (Kutch, Gujarat) was selected as a UNWTO Best Tourism Village in 2023, recognised for community-based tourism, promotion of the Rann Utsav cultural festival, and rural livelihood support. UNESCO administers heritage listings and the Creative Cities Network — it does not run this 'Best Tourism Village' award. UNEP focuses on environmental programmes, and the WTTC runs a separate Tourism for Tomorrow award. Confusing UNWTO with UNESCO is the most common exam-day error on this question.

questions.stem: The Akal Wood Fossil Park near Jaisalmer preserves petrified tree trunks of the genus Sonaroxylon, which are scientifically significant because they establish that the present-day Thar Desert region was once covered by:

options.option_text: A tropical or sub-tropical forest approximately 180 million years ago in the Jurassic period
A continental glacial ice sheet approximately 65 million years ago in the Cretaceous period
A vast inland freshwater lake approximately 10,000 years ago during the Holocene epoch
A shallow marine coral reef system approximately 500 million years ago in the Cambrian era

questions.explanation: The Akal Wood Fossil Park (17 km from Jaisalmer) contains petrified conifer logs dating to approximately 180 million years (Late Jurassic), proving the Thar was then a humid forest. The fossils are classified as Sonaroxylon rajasthanensis. A Cretaceous glaciation in peninsular India is inconsistent with its tectonic position near the equator at that time. A Holocene lake 10,000 years ago would not produce stone-fossils of tree trunks. Cambrian coral reefs predate these fossils by 300+ million years and are not evidenced at Akal.

questions.stem: In desert geomorphology, a 'barchan' dune differs from a 'seif' (longitudinal) dune primarily in that a barchan:

options.option_text: Forms parallel to the dominant wind direction and extends for hundreds of kilometres
Is crescent-shaped, migrates downwind, and forms where sand supply is limited
Is a flat, salt-encrusted surface that remains after a desert playa lake evaporates
Is a star-shaped multi-armed dune built by converging multi-directional wind regimes

questions.explanation: A barchan is a crescent-shaped dune with two forward-pointing horns; it forms under a consistent unidirectional wind where sand supply is sparse, and migrates downwind — barchans are common in the Thar. A seif (longitudinal) dune, by contrast, runs parallel to the dominant wind for hundreds of km (Option A describes a seif). Option C describes a playa or takyr, not a dune form. Option D describes a star dune (rhourd), which forms under multi-directional winds with abundant sand — the opposite supply condition to a barchan.
